newsitem.title: PERU: U.S. says it gave no support to Peru's commandos.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says it gave no support to Peru's commandos.

text.p: The United States gave no support or advice to the Peruvian forces who raided the besieged Japanese diplomatic compound in Lima because Peru did not ask for it, U.S. ambassador Dennis Jett said on Wednesday.
"The military incursion was carried out by the Peruvian government ... Peru never asked for anything from us," Jett was quoted as saying by local news agency Andina.
Jett said he believed the raid, in which one hostage, two commandos and all 14 hostage-takers died, followed sincere efforts by President Alberto Fujimori to reach a negotiated solution.
"We think that the government of Peru tried to find a peaceful solution. Since that was not possible, the matter ended the way it did yesterday," he was quoted as saying.

A State Department spokesman, Nicholas Burns, said in Washington that the United States had no advance warning of the raid but had gained "some indications" that an assault on the residence was afoot and that the United States played no role.
"Did we provide training for the raid, for the military assault team? No. Did we ever provide training to the military assault team? No," Burns said.

The United States sent a contingency team to Lima soon after the residence takeover on Dec. 17 because six Americans were among the 500 original hostages. The Americans were released soon afterward and the team returned to Washington in early January.
